theFinding.statement: Only 3 of the 6 counties hold property-boundary-edge atoms: Bastrop 3,732 parcels, Caldwell 6,482, Hays 48,611. McLennan, Travis AND Williamson hold ZERO, under the live readers' own bind, in the store they serve from, corroborated by a positive control returning the expected 9 edges.
theFinding.divergence: The dispatch's trap list names McLennan only ('McLennan has 0 boundary atoms county-wide'). Travis and Williamson are not named, and Travis is a primary county.
theFinding.whyItBlocksThePolicyMoveFOrParcelGeometr: `refused` is an earned cell kind, so a county whose parcelGeometry cells are ALL `refused atom-miss` still produces a rail verdict of `pass` (zero unaccounted, at least one earned). Cutting the rail over to must-pass would let three counties read COMPLETE on a rail for which they hold no boundary geometry -- the silent-completion shape P-252 closed one level up. The writer's behaviour is right (A-214 makes an absence the wrong cell); the POLICY move is premature for that rail.

threeQuestionGate.whatExecutesTheWriterAndTheReader: WRITER: nothing executes it yet -- deliberately. This lane lands the decision core only. The planned chain, which the repo's own controls check in both directions, is one job module in src/jobs/, one entry in writer-allowlist.mjs, one branch in src/cli.mjs, and one cloudbuild deploy target; plus a DESTRUCTIVE_WRITERS register row importing src/lib/destructive-write-guard.mjs, and the heavy-scan lease. The statement that writes the cell is deliberately NOT in the landed module (see its header): landing it in a planner would buy a register row describing a non-writer. READER: hauska-engine services/retrieval-api/src/parcel-record-reader.ts, which consults parcel-record-slate.json for each (county, rail) pair. Today 0 of the 18 pairs are slated, so for these three rails nothing serves from the ledger at all -- the customer keeps reading the pre-cutover path (LDT's atoms, and hauska-map's panel for ETJ).
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersThem: WRITER: a COUNTY RUN -- it is a set-valued county writer (one county per invocation), dry-run by default, writing only on --apply, under the heavy-scan lease and the destructive-write guard. Not a per-parcel trigger, and not a schedule of its own. READER: request-driven -- an HTTP request to the retrieval-api, with the slate deciding per (county, rail) whether the ledger or the pre-cutover path answers. The GRADING leg that consumes the cells is the scheduled one: publish-gate-sched.mjs -> gate-rail-cli.mjs -> the pinned per-rail gate, which writes parcel_gate_verdict on a schedule.
threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenACellDisagreesWithItsSource: NOTHING TODAY, and this is the strongest open item this lane found. The gate grades cell KINDS, not cell values: evaluateRailGate returns ok on 'no unaccounted cells and at least one earned cell', and never compares a cell to the atom it was written from. So a cell that goes stale -- an atom retired after its cell was written, a re-fetched pipeline fact whose boolean changed -- keeps serving and keeps grading. Worse, the write gate (only unaccounted cells change) is what makes that permanent: the writer as designed is CREATE-ONLY and cannot refresh an earned cell. The nearest controls are the atom-side readers' own refusal codes (bind-conflict, malformed-atom) which the cell now mirrors, and the divergence guard on the slate -- neither of which compares cell to source. A refresh/reconcile path needs a ruling about what may overwrite an earned cell; naming it is this lane's job, not solving it.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypassesThem: 1) The customer path today IS the bypass: LDT/cortex-api serve group A and hauska-map serves ETJ from the atoms and the determination directly, so a customer reads a value with no ledger cell in the path -- which is why 'cells written' is not 'cut over' and why the slate, not the cell, is the serve switch. 2) A hand-written parcel_gate_verdict row bypasses the gate entirely (classifyExclusion states the same hazard for its own input). 3) A caller reaching the vendored per-rail gate directly never passes through gate-exclusion-classifier.mjs. 4) An unslated pair keeps its pre-cutover path forever (A-193), so a rail can be fully written, graded pass, and still not serve.

leaveBehind: THE READER LEG IS CROSS-REPO AND ORDERED, not an engine change. The engine's slate is a byte-pinned vendored copy of LDT's PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE literal whose both-directions divergence guard fails on an invented pair, and its own history records the rule for adding one: a pair is added only once its parcel_gate_verdict reads `pass` in the production store. So the order is (1) writer applied, verdicts flip to pass; (2) 18 pairs added to legacy-design-tools artifacts/api-server/src/lib/parcelRecordAllowlist.ts; (3) doc_repo scripts/p299_slate_revendor.mjs re-vendors FOUR places as one fact (the JSON, EXPECTED_SLATE_HASH, the LDT literal fixture, its digest); (4) the engine reader then serves them. Until (2)-(3), the cells exist and grade while the customer keeps reading the pre-cutover path.
